scope: Actual individual page images 11 through 20 only; no approval or visual claims about the other PDF pages.
view_method: Each assigned PNG was opened separately with functions.view_image detail=original and emitted as an image, not inferred from extracted text or a contact sheet.

findings.region: Bottom of page, after the Feature transport and the Treasury failure paragraph
findings.description: The Table 8 caption is at the foot of page 11, while its table header and all rows begin on page 12. The caption itself is readable and unclipped, but its separation from the table is an avoidable pagination defect.
findings.suggested_repair: Keep the Table 8 caption together with at least its header and first row, without changing any table values.

observations: The continued aggregate-panel table repeats its header and fits the page width.
Table 11 has readable source/H/W and FHS/Peak POT/QRF loss-change and hit columns; the NA issued-count labels are visible.
Delta symbols and table rule lines render, and the body has no visible clipping or missing glyph boxes.
Table 11 precedes the preserved Table 8 label in reading order; this was noted without changing labels or asserting a numerical contradiction.
Table 8 starts with its column header and all eight rows remain together, but its caption is on the preceding page.
The compact numeric columns, lambda, negative signs, percentages and COMPLETE labels remain within their columns.
The limitations paragraphs continue cleanly to the lower margin without clipping or visible math-glyph loss.
Conclusion heading and all three paragraphs are readable and intact.
The adverse Treasury primary, breach increases, panel negatives and numerical exclusions remain explicitly visible.
The remaining white space before the separately started references is not clipped or missing content.
Reference entries wrap within the margins, including long titles and the Barone-Adesi DOI containing angle brackets.
The Hansch, Ho and Lyons entries display their DOI numbers in visible text.
Journal italics, accented names and page ranges are legible; no reference line is visibly clipped.
The remaining reference entries wrap cleanly and are fully readable.
The Ito-Nisio accent and other diacritics are visible without replacement boxes.
No citation entry is cut off at the bottom; unused space is a deliberate section boundary rather than a rendering failure.
Appendix A and sections A.1/A.2 have dense but readable text and clear headings.
Absolute-value bars, inequalities, min/max indices, positive/negative anchor cases and the signed-anchor scripts render visibly.
The mathematical displays fit horizontally; the final text remains above the page number without overlap.
Table A1 and Table A2 retain their captions, headers and rows on the same page.
Ceiling/rank notation, tau, phi, superscript powers and the raw-translation tilde are visible.
The A.4 path-difference display and bound fit the page width and have no visible missing glyphs or script collision.
The two Appendix B tables have adjacent captions and repeat their meaningful source-unit and loss-difference labels.
Plus/minus signs, decimal values, F-minus-S headings and sensitivity-setting labels are readable and within column boundaries.
The preserved adverse historical outcomes and the resampling interpretation limits remain visibly intact.
The numerical-conventions and equivalent-peak-parameterization sections fit with comfortable lower-page space.
Summation signs, rho, beta, lambda, kappa, mu, theta, subscripts, superscripts, norms and dual/primal equations render without missing boxes.
The shifted-penalty display and floor projection are readable; no display is clipped at either margin.
Table D1 caption, header and twelve rows remain together and fit the page width.
Long Treasury maximum-gap entries and the FX/Treasury unit qualification are legible.
The bottom equation shows the integral, alpha limits and powers without missing glyphs, clipping or contact with the page number.

boundary: Visual checks cover appearance and visible labels on pages 11-20. They do not establish numerical correctness, provenance, statistical validity, successful TeX compilation, or acceptance of other pages.
